requirements.text: A bound-stopped turn's single retry targets the next tier above the model that was actually running, not the configured escalate tier.
A Luna turn retries on subscription Terra `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra` with medium thinking when that exact id resolves in the session registry.
When subscription Terra does not resolve, a Luna turn retries on subscription Sol `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with high thinking if that exact id resolves.
A Terra turn retries on subscription Sol `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with high thinking when that exact id resolves.
A Sol turn, an unknown model family, or a turn with no resolvable subscription target does not retry; the bound stops and reports normally.
No retry may target a per-token provider; model family recognition is provider-independent, but every returned target uses the `openai-codex` subscription provider.
At most one bound retry is allowed per original prompt.
The existing SPEC-delegation-ab §3.1 bound checkpoint line remains the retry prompt.
`lib/tiers.ts` exports `nextTier(model, resolves)`, returning a target model/thinking pair or null.
`lib/tiers.ts` exports `retryAllowed({ env, held, alreadyRetried })`, which permits a retry only when the switch is enabled, no quota hold exists, and the original prompt has not already retried.
`extensions/bounds.ts` delegates retry policy to both `nextTier` and `retryAllowed` rather than duplicating their decisions.
`extensions/bounds.ts` computes quota hold state as `readHold(defaultHoldPath(process.env)) !== null`; any hold blocks the retry.
`PI_BUILD_RETRY=0` disables retry entirely, including for pinned measurements; other values or absence of the variable do not disable it by themselves.
The delivered `tiers.test.ts` must pass, and an implementer-owned bounds test must show a bound retry selecting through `nextTier` and being blocked while a quota hold exists.
`bin/pi-rework <spec> <task|*> <reason...>` records one rework finding with the full remaining argument text as its reason.
`bin/pi-rework --list [spec]` lists rework findings for the current repository, optionally filtered by normalized spec name.

The rework command is intended to be run whenever spec-driven work is found wrong or incomplete and must be redone, whether found immediately or days later; logging may be incomplete, but every recorded row is retained as the production silent-failure signal.
A spec argument may be a spec name, `SPEC-` name, file name, or path, and all forms normalize to the name used by `docs/SPEC-<name>.md` and its plan directory.

A task argument is either an id present in that spec's plan or `*`; `*` denotes a finding for the whole spec, including integration failures and underspecified specs, and remains valid when no plan exists.
The reason is required, non-whitespace free text.
Recording refuses a spec whose `docs/SPEC-<name>.md` file does not exist.
Recording refuses a task id not present in the spec plan, lists the valid task ids and `*`, and appends no unjoinable row.
A non-`*` task is refused when the spec has no plan; a malformed plan supplies no valid task ids rather than bypassing validation.

Rows are JSON Lines at `~/.pi/agent/rework.jsonl` by default (overridable with `PI_BUILD_REWORK`) and every row contains normalized spec, task, reason, ISO time, and the repository root so one user-level log can serve multiple projects.
Only spec-driven work is loggable with a task id because ids are validated against `docs/SPEC-<name>.plan/plan.json`; whole-spec findings use `*`.
The delivered `rework.test.ts` must pass, and `bin/pi-rework` must record a row whose spec and task fields can be joined to the plan/results data used by the §5.3 report.

tasks.brief: Create only `lib/tiers.ts`. Read `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §2, `docs/SPEC-production-config.tests/tiers.test.ts`, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.reference/lib/tiers.ts`; the reference is guidance, but this brief is the complete contract. Do not edit the delivered spec test, the reference tree, `extensions/bounds.ts`, settings, or any other file. Export exactly these public declarations: `type Family = "luna" | "terra" | "sol"`; `interface RetryTarget { model: string; thinking: "medium" | "high"; }`; `const CODEX` with readonly values `terra: "openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra"` and `sol: "openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol"`; `familyOf(model: string): Family | null`; `nextTier(model: string, resolves: (id: string) => boolean): RetryTarget | null`; and `retryAllowed(input: { env: Record<string, string | undefined>; held: boolean; alreadyRetried: boolean }): boolean`. The two CODEX values are constants because retries must use the subscription provider and must never silently spend per-token dollars. `familyOf` recognizes only model names ending exactly in `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, or `gpt-5.6-sol`; ignore any provider prefix, and return null for every other model. The applicable reading of 'next tier' is: Luna asks `resolves` for subscription Terra first and returns it with medium thinking; if Terra does not resolve, Luna asks for subscription Sol and returns it with high thinking; Terra asks only for subscription Sol with high thinking; Sol and unknown families return null; if a required subscription id does not resolve, return null. Never probe or return `openai/...` per-token ids. `retryAllowed` returns false exactly when `env.PI_BUILD_RETRY === "0"`, `held` is true, or `alreadyRetried` is true; otherwise it returns true. Here 'already retried' means the one retry for the original prompt, not one retry per bound event. Keep this module pure and independent of pi APIs, filesystem state, settings, and quota reads; those belong to `extensions/bounds.ts`.

Edit only `extensions/bounds.ts`. Read the whole existing file, `lib/tiers.ts` from T1, `lib/quota.ts`, `lib/telemetry.ts` for `claimBoundRetry`/checkpoint state, `lib/models.ts` only where registry model references must be split, `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §2, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.tests/tiers.test.ts`. Replace the old configured-escalate retry choice with the tier policy from `nextTier`, and call `retryAllowed({ env: process.env, held, alreadyRetried })` for the gate. Preserve the current checkpoint text from `boundCheckpointLine` as the follow-up retry prompt, preserve one retry per original prompt through the existing `claimBoundRetry` mechanism, and preserve normal bound checkpoint/report/abort behavior when no target resolves or retry is disallowed. Compute `held` exactly as `readHold(defaultHoldPath(process.env)) !== null`. Resolution must be an exact registry lookup of the subscription target returned by `nextTier`; split the returned `provider/id` only for `ctx.modelRegistry.find(provider, id)`, then set that exact model and its returned medium/high thinking value. Pass `${ctx.model.provider}/${ctx.model.id}` to `nextTier`, because `ctx.model` is the model actually running at the bound; do not infer the family from routing settings, the active-tier label, or `defaultModel`. If `ctx.model` or the registry is absent, no retry is possible. Do not add per-token fallback, do not change routing configuration, telemetry schemas, quota behavior, queue text/source, unrelated bound limits, or any other file. Existing exports and signatures must remain: default `boundsExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI): Promise<void>`, `firstUnwrittenPath(noteText: string | null, written: string[]): string`, `boundCheckpointLine(reason: string, written: string[], resumeFrom: string): string`, `runBoundAbort(input): Promise<void>`, and `checkpointOnBound(input): Promise<void>`.

Edit only `tests/bounds-split.test.ts`. Read the existing test, the completed `extensions/bounds.ts`, `lib/tiers.ts`, `lib/quota.ts`, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §2. Keep unrelated bounds tests. Replace the old assertion that a retry always uses configured escalate with behavioral coverage showing the running Luna model retries through `nextTier` to exact subscription Terra at medium thinking, fallback to subscription Sol occurs when Terra is absent, and the existing checkpoint line is sent. Keep or strengthen the tests that a second bound for the same original prompt does not retry, `PI_BUILD_RETRY=0` blocks retry, and a real quota hold at `defaultHoldPath(process.env)` blocks retry. Include a no-target/Sol case that still aborts and reports without setting a model. Assertions must observe extension behavior through the fake pi/model registry; do not assert source text or private helper implementation. Do not edit author tests under `docs/SPEC-production-config.tests/`, production code, or any other test file.

Create only `lib/rework.ts`. Read `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §5.2, `docs/SPEC-production-config.tests/rework.test.ts`, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.reference/lib/rework.ts`; the reference is guidance, but this brief is the complete contract. Do not edit the delivered test, the reference tree, CLI files, or any other file. Export exactly: `interface ReworkRow { spec: string; task: string; reason: string; at: string; project: string; }`; `const WHOLE_SPEC = "*"`; `defaultReworkPath(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string`; `normalizeSpecName(input: string): string`; `planTaskIds(plan: unknown): string[]`; `type Validation = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string }`; `validateRework(input: { spec: string; task: string; reason: string }, specExists: boolean, taskIds: string[] | null): Validation`; `appendRework(path: string, row: ReworkRow): void`; and `readRework(path: string): ReworkRow[]`. `WHOLE_SPEC` is `"*"` because that is the command's sentinel for integration or underspecified whole-spec findings. `PI_BUILD_REWORK` is the sole path override; otherwise use the current user's `~/.pi/agent/rework.jsonl`, so one log serves all repositories and each row's `project` disambiguates them. Normalize a path, `.md` file name, `SPEC-` name, or bare name by trimming, taking the final slash-separated component, removing a case-insensitive `.md` suffix, then removing an initial uppercase `SPEC-`; do not require the file to exist in this pure helper. `planTaskIds` returns string ids from an object with an array `tasks`, skips malformed entries, and returns `[]` for malformed input. In validation, reject a missing spec first, then a whitespace-only reason; accept `*` whether task ids are an array or null. The applicable reading of no plan is: null permits only `*`; an empty array means a plan existed but exposed no valid ids. Reject every other unknown task and put all valid ids plus `*` in the error so typos cannot append unjoinable rows. `appendRework` creates parent directories and appends exactly one JSON object plus newline without replacing prior findings. `readRework` returns `[]` for an absent file, parses JSON lines in order, skips blank/malformed lines, and returns rows with string spec/task/reason fields; logging is append-only and need not prove that every real-world rework event was captured.

Create only `scripts/pi-rework.ts`. Read `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §5.2, completed `lib/rework.ts`, `docs/SPEC-production-config.tests/rework.test.ts`, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.reference/scripts/pi-rework.ts`. Do not edit any of those files, the wrapper under `bin/`, plans/specs, or the log during implementation tests except through a temporary `PI_BUILD_REWORK` path. This is a command module and exports no names. Import and use these exact T4 interfaces rather than duplicating them: `interface ReworkRow { spec: string; task: string; reason: string; at: string; project: string; }`; `appendRework(path: string, row: ReworkRow): void`; `defaultReworkPath(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string`; `normalizeSpecName(input: string): string`; `planTaskIds(plan: unknown): string[]`; `readRework(path: string): ReworkRow[]`; `type Validation = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string }`; and `validateRework(input: { spec: string; task: string; reason: string }, specExists: boolean, taskIds: string[] | null): Validation`. Determine repository root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to `process.cwd()` only when git cannot resolve it. Constants and fixed values: recording success/list success exit 0; validation failure exit 1; malformed command usage exit 2, because 2 distinguishes invocation syntax from a rejected finding; spec paths are `<root>/docs/SPEC-<normalized>.md`; plans are `<root>/docs/SPEC-<normalized>.plan/plan.json`; each row timestamp is `new Date().toISOString()`; and the log path comes from `defaultReworkPath(process.env)`. Recording syntax is `<spec> <task|*> <reason...>`; join every argument after task with a single space as free-text reason. Fewer than three recording arguments prints both supported forms and exits 2. A present parseable plan supplies `planTaskIds`; an absent plan supplies null; a present malformed plan supplies an empty id list, so it cannot bypass task validation. Validate before appending. On failure print the validation error and append nothing. On success append `{ spec, task, reason, at, project: root }` and print a concise confirmation. `--list [spec]` reads the shared log, keeps only rows whose `project` exactly equals the current root, optionally filters by `normalizeSpecName`, prints each finding with timestamp/spec/task/reason, and prints `No rework recorded.` when empty. The applicable reading of `--list [spec]` is repository-local output even though storage is user-global. Do not add credential access, telemetry writes, report generation, automatic completeness checks, or acceptance of non-plan task ids.

Create only the executable file `bin/pi-rework`. Read completed `scripts/pi-rework.ts`, existing `bin/pi-continue` for repository wrapper style, `docs/SPEC-production-config.md` §5.2, and `docs/SPEC-production-config.reference/bin/pi-rework`. Do not edit the TypeScript command, any other wrapper, specs, tests, plans, or settings. This wrapper exports no names. It must be a bash script with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and replace itself via `exec` with `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/pi-rework.ts" "$@"`. The node flags are fixed because the target is TypeScript and routine CLI output must not include Node's experimental warning; `exec` is required so callers receive the command's exact exit status and signals; `"$@"` is required so spec, task, and multiword reason arguments are forwarded without loss. Mark the file executable. The applicable reading of the two documented `bin/pi-rework` forms is that this wrapper performs no validation itself; all behavior belongs to the script.
